cards.front: Where do the three main long tracts of the spinal cord cross the midline?
cards.back: **Dorsal columns** (fine touch, vibration, proprioception): in the **medulla**. **Spinothalamic tract** (pain, temperature): in the cord, via the **anterior white commissure**, within 1-2 segments of entry. **Lateral corticospinal tract** (motor): at the **pyramidal decussation** in the lower medulla.
cards.back_pt: **Colunas dorsais** (tato fino, vibração, propriocepção): no **bulbo**. **Trato espinotalâmico** (dor, temperatura): na medula, pela **comissura branca anterior**, em até 1-2 segmentos da entrada. **Trato corticoespinhal lateral** (motor): na **decussação das pirâmides**, na parte inferior do bulbo.

cards.front: Why is a lumbar puncture done at L3-L4 or L4-L5, and which layers does the needle cross?
cards.back: The cord ends at the **conus medullaris** (L1-L2 in adults); the iliac crests mark about **L4**. Layers: skin, subcutaneous tissue, supraspinous and interspinous ligaments, **ligamentum flavum**, epidural space, **dura**, **arachnoid**, then CSF in the subarachnoid space.
cards.back_pt: A medula termina no **cone medular** (L1-L2 no adulto); as cristas ilíacas marcam cerca de **L4**. Camadas: pele, tecido subcutâneo, ligamentos supraespinal e interespinal, **ligamento amarelo**, espaço epidural, **dura-máter**, **aracnoide** e então o LCR no espaço subaracnóideo.

cards.front: How do upper motor neuron (UMN) and lower motor neuron (LMN) lesions differ on exam?
cards.back: **UMN**: weakness with **spasticity**, **hyperreflexia** and a **Babinski sign**; little atrophy. **LMN**: **flaccid** weakness, **hyporeflexia**, marked **atrophy** and **fasciculations**; plantar response is normal (flexor).
cards.back_pt: **NMS**: fraqueza com **espasticidade**, **hiper-reflexia** e **sinal de Babinski**; pouca atrofia. **NMI**: fraqueza **flácida**, **hiporreflexia**, **atrofia** acentuada e **fasciculações**; o reflexo cutâneo-plantar é normal (em flexão).

cards.front: Why does syringomyelia cause a cape-like loss of pain and temperature with preserved touch?
cards.back: A fluid cavity (**syrinx**) in the central cervical cord damages the **spinothalamic fibers crossing in the anterior white commissure**. The **dorsal columns are spared**. Often linked to **Chiari I malformation**; a growing syrinx can hit anterior horns (hand atrophy).
cards.back_pt: Uma cavidade líquida (**siringe**) na região central da medula cervical lesa as **fibras espinotalâmicas que cruzam na comissura branca anterior**. As **colunas dorsais são poupadas**. Associa-se muitas vezes à **malformação de Chiari tipo I**; uma siringe que cresce pode atingir os cornos anteriores (atrofia das mãos).

cards.front: How does a conus medullaris lesion differ from cauda equina syndrome?
cards.back: **Conus medullaris**: often sudden and **symmetric**, with **early bladder and bowel dysfunction**, little radicular pain, and possible mixed UMN and LMN signs. **Cauda equina**: roots only, so pure **LMN** signs; often **asymmetric**, with severe **radicular pain** and later sphincter loss. Both can cause **saddle anesthesia**.
cards.back_pt: **Cone medular**: geralmente súbito e **simétrico**, com **disfunção vesical e intestinal precoce**, pouca dor radicular e possível mistura de sinais de NMS e NMI. **Cauda equina**: só raízes, então sinais puros de **NMI**; geralmente **assimétrica**, com **dor radicular** intensa e perda esfincteriana mais tardia. Ambas podem causar **anestesia em sela**.

cards.front: Which part of the brachial plexus is injured in Erb palsy, and what posture results?
cards.back: **Upper trunk (C5-C6)**, from traction that widens the neck-shoulder angle (e.g., shoulder dystocia). The arm hangs **adducted** and **internally rotated**, with the **elbow extended** and the **forearm pronated**: the *waiter's tip* posture.
cards.back_pt: **Tronco superior (C5-C6)**, por tração que aumenta o ângulo entre pescoço e ombro (ex.: distocia de ombro). O braço fica **aduzido** e em **rotação interna**, com o **cotovelo estendido** e o **antebraço pronado**: a postura em *waiter's tip* ("gorjeta de garçom").

cards.front: Which nerve is at risk with a fracture of each part of the humerus?
cards.back: **Surgical neck**: **axillary nerve** (weak deltoid, numb lateral shoulder). **Midshaft** (radial groove): **radial nerve** (**wrist drop**). **Supracondylar**: **median nerve** (and brachial artery). **Medial epicondyle**: **ulnar nerve** (weak finger abduction, ulnar claw).
cards.back_pt: **Colo cirúrgico**: **nervo axilar** (deltoide fraco, dormência na face lateral do ombro). **Diáfise** (sulco do nervo radial): **nervo radial** (**mão caída**). **Supracondiliana**: **nervo mediano** (e artéria braquial). **Epicôndilo medial**: **nervo ulnar** (abdução dos dedos fraca, garra ulnar).

cards.front: What sign follows injury to the superior gluteal nerve?
cards.back: Weak **gluteus medius and minimus** (hip abductors). Standing on the **affected** leg, the pelvis drops on the **opposite** side: a positive **Trendelenburg sign**. A classic cause is an intramuscular injection placed in the upper medial buttock instead of the upper lateral quadrant.
cards.back_pt: Fraqueza dos **glúteos médio e mínimo** (abdutores do quadril). Em apoio sobre a perna **afetada**, a pelve cai do lado **oposto**: **sinal de Trendelenburg** positivo. Uma causa clássica é uma injeção intramuscular aplicada na parte superomedial da nádega, em vez do quadrante superolateral.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man is examined 3 weeks after a stab wound to the back. He still cannot move his right leg well. Exam shows weakness of the right leg with brisk right knee and ankle reflexes and an extensor plantar response on the right. Vibration and joint position sense are lost in the right leg. Pain and temperature sensation are lost in the left leg and the left side of the trunk below the level of the umbilicus. Arm strength and sensation are normal. Which lesion best explains these findings?
choices: Hemisection of the left side of the thoracic spinal cord
Infarction of the anterior two-thirds of the thoracic spinal cord
Hemisection of the right side of the thoracic spinal cord
A fluid-filled cavity in the central gray matter of the thoracic cord
Infarction of the left medial medulla
questions.explanation: This is **Brown-Séquard syndrome** from a **right** hemisection. The lateral corticospinal tract and dorsal columns cross in the medulla, so motor and vibration/position loss are **ipsilateral**. The spinothalamic tract crosses within 1-2 segments of entry, so pain and temperature loss is **contralateral** and starts slightly below the lesion. A left hemisection is tempting because the pain loss is on the left, but the weakness and dorsal column loss point to the right; a left medial medullary infarct would also weaken the right arm and spare pain and temperature.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se da **síndrome de Brown-Séquard** por hemissecção **direita**. O trato corticoespinhal lateral e as colunas dorsais cruzam no bulbo, então a perda motora e a de vibração/posição são **ipsilaterais**. O trato espinotalâmico cruza em até 1-2 segmentos da entrada, então a perda de dor e temperatura é **contralateral** e começa um pouco abaixo da lesão. Uma hemissecção esquerda é tentadora porque a perda de dor está à esquerda, mas a fraqueza e a perda das colunas dorsais apontam para a direita; um infarto bulbar medial esquerdo também enfraqueceria o braço direito e pouparia dor e temperatura.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man is kicked on the outer side of his left knee during a soccer game. An x-ray shows a fracture of the neck of the left fibula. On exam, he cannot dorsiflex or evert the left foot. Plantar flexion and inversion are normal, and the ankle and knee reflexes are normal. He has numbness over the dorsum of the foot. When he walks, he lifts the left knee high so the toes do not catch the floor. Which nerve is most likely injured?
choices: Tibial nerve
Common fibular (peroneal) nerve
Sciatic nerve
Femoral nerve
Superior gluteal nerve
questions.explanation: The **common fibular nerve** wraps around the **fibular neck**, where it is easily injured. Loss of its deep branch causes **foot drop** (no dorsiflexion) and a **steppage gait**; loss of its superficial branch weakens eversion and numbs the dorsum of the foot. A **sciatic** injury would also cause foot drop, but it would weaken plantar flexion and inversion (tibial part) and reduce the ankle reflex, which are normal here.
questions.explanation_pt: O **nervo fibular comum** contorna o **colo da fíbula**, onde é facilmente lesado. A perda do ramo profundo causa **pé caído** (sem dorsiflexão) e **marcha escarvante**; a perda do ramo superficial enfraquece a eversão e causa dormência no dorso do pé. Uma lesão do **nervo isquiático** também causaria pé caído, mas enfraqueceria a flexão plantar e a inversão (componente tibial) e reduziria o reflexo aquileu, que estão normais aqui.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old woman with hypothyroidism and vitiligo has 6 months of tingling in her feet and an unsteady gait that is worse in the dark. Exam shows loss of vibration and joint position sense in both feet and a positive Romberg sign. Both legs are mildly weak and spastic, knee reflexes are brisk, and both plantar responses are extensor. Hemoglobin is 9.6 g/dL and mean corpuscular volume is 114 fL. The blood smear shows hypersegmented neutrophils. Which parts of the spinal cord are most likely damaged?
choices: Dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts
Dorsal columns and dorsal roots only
Anterior horns and lateral corticospinal tracts
Anterior white commissure in the cervical cord
Anterior two-thirds of the cord with sparing of the dorsal columns
questions.explanation: Autoimmune disease, macrocytic anemia and hypersegmented neutrophils suggest **vitamin B12 deficiency** from pernicious anemia. B12 deficiency causes **subacute combined degeneration**: demyelination of the **dorsal columns** (vibration and position loss, Romberg sign) and the **lateral corticospinal tracts** (spasticity, hyperreflexia, Babinski). **Tabes dorsalis** also damages the dorsal columns and roots, but it causes no UMN signs and does not cause megaloblastic anemia.
questions.explanation_pt: Doença autoimune, anemia macrocítica e neutrófilos hipersegmentados sugerem **deficiência de vitamina B12** por anemia perniciosa. A deficiência de B12 causa **degeneração combinada subaguda**: desmielinização das **colunas dorsais** (perda de vibração e posição, sinal de Romberg) e dos **tratos corticoespinhais laterais** (espasticidade, hiper-reflexia, Babinski). A **tabes dorsalis** também lesa as colunas e raízes dorsais, mas não causa sinais de NMS nem anemia megaloblástica.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man has low back pain that started while lifting a heavy box 2 weeks ago. The pain shoots down the back of his right thigh and calf to the outer edge of the foot and the little toe. He has reduced sensation along the lateral border of the right foot. He has difficulty standing on the toes of his right foot. The right Achilles reflex is absent. The patellar reflexes and great toe dorsiflexion are normal. Which nerve root is most likely compressed?
choices: L2
L3
L4
L5
S1
questions.explanation: The **S1** root supplies the **lateral foot and little toe**, **plantar flexion** (standing on the toes) and the **Achilles reflex** (S1-S2). **L5** is the most tempting choice, but L5 compression weakens **great toe and foot dorsiflexion**, numbs the dorsum of the foot, and usually leaves the Achilles reflex intact. L4 would reduce the patellar reflex (L3-L4), which is normal here.
questions.explanation_pt: A raiz **S1** inerva a **borda lateral do pé e o quinto dedo**, a **flexão plantar** (ficar na ponta dos pés) e o **reflexo aquileu** (S1-S2). **L5** é a opção mais tentadora, mas a compressão de L5 enfraquece a **dorsiflexão do hálux e do pé**, causa dormência no dorso do pé e geralmente preserva o reflexo aquileu. L4 reduziria o reflexo patelar (L3-L4), que está normal aqui.

notes.title: Spinal cord and peripheral nerves: tracts, lesions and nerve injuries
notes.body_md:
## Tracts

- **Dorsal columns** (touch, vibration, proprioception): cross in the **medulla**.
- **Spinothalamic** (pain, temperature): cross in the cord within 1-2 segments.
- **Lateral corticospinal** (motor): cross at the **pyramidal decussation**.

## Cord lesions

- **Brown-Séquard** (hemisection): ipsilateral weakness and dorsal column loss; contralateral pain and temperature loss.
- **Syringomyelia**: bilateral **cape-like** pain and temperature loss, touch spared; linked to **Chiari I**.
- **Anterior spinal artery** occlusion: bilateral weakness and pain/temperature loss, **dorsal columns spared**; can follow aortic surgery.
- **Subacute combined degeneration** (B12): dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts.
- **Anterior horn** loss (poliomyelitis, Werdnig-Hoffmann): pure LMN signs.
- ALS and Guillain-Barré: see the neurodegenerative block. Tabes dorsalis: see the STI block.

## UMN vs LMN

- **UMN**: spasticity, hyperreflexia, **Babinski sign**.
- **LMN**: flaccid weakness, hyporeflexia, atrophy, **fasciculations**.

## Levels

- Reflexes: biceps C5-C6, triceps C7-C8, patellar L3-L4, Achilles S1-S2.
- Cord ends at the **conus medullaris** (L1-L2); lumbar puncture at L3-L4 or L4-L5.
- **Conus** lesion: early, symmetric bladder and bowel loss. **Cauda equina**: asymmetric radicular pain, pure LMN signs, later sphincter loss. Both can cause saddle anesthesia.

## Upper limb

- **Erb** (upper trunk, C5-C6): *waiter's tip*. **Klumpke** (lower trunk, C8-T1): claw hand, sometimes Horner syndrome.
- **Thoracic outlet** (e.g., cervical rib): lower trunk and subclavian vessels.
- **Long thoracic** nerve: **winged scapula**.
- Humerus: surgical neck, **axillary**; midshaft, **radial** (wrist drop); supracondylar, **median**. Medial epicondyle: **ulnar** (ulnar claw). Carpal tunnel: median.

## Lower limb

- **Common fibular** (fibular neck): **foot drop**.
- **Tibial**: weak plantar flexion. **Femoral**: weak knee extension, lost patellar reflex.
- **Sciatic**: both fibular and tibial deficits.
- **Superior gluteal**: **Trendelenburg sign**.

## Neuropathy

- **Axonal**: low amplitude, near-normal conduction velocity.
- **Demyelinating**: slow conduction velocity.
- Diabetic neuropathy: see the diabetes block.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Tratos

- **Colunas dorsais** (tato, vibração, propriocepção): cruzam no **bulbo**.
- **Espinotalâmico** (dor, temperatura): cruza na medula em até 1-2 segmentos.
- **Corticoespinhal lateral** (motor): cruza na **decussação das pirâmides**.

## Lesões medulares

- **Brown-Séquard** (hemissecção): fraqueza e perda das colunas dorsais ipsilaterais; perda de dor e temperatura contralateral.
- **Siringomielia**: perda bilateral de dor e temperatura **em capa**, tato poupado; associada a **Chiari I**.
- Oclusão da **artéria espinhal anterior**: fraqueza e perda de dor/temperatura bilaterais, **colunas dorsais poupadas**; pode ocorrer após cirurgia de aorta.
- **Degeneração combinada subaguda** (B12): colunas dorsais e tratos corticoespinhais laterais.
- Perda do **corno anterior** (poliomielite, Werdnig-Hoffmann): sinais puros de NMI.
- ELA e Guillain-Barré: ver o bloco neurodegenerativo. Tabes dorsalis: ver o bloco de IST.

## NMS vs NMI

- **NMS**: espasticidade, hiper-reflexia, **sinal de Babinski**.
- **NMI**: fraqueza flácida, hiporreflexia, atrofia, **fasciculações**.

## Níveis

- Reflexos: bicipital C5-C6, tricipital C7-C8, patelar L3-L4, aquileu S1-S2.
- A medula termina no **cone medular** (L1-L2); punção lombar em L3-L4 ou L4-L5.
- Lesão do **cone**: perda vesical e intestinal precoce e simétrica. **Cauda equina**: dor radicular assimétrica, sinais puros de NMI, perda esfincteriana mais tardia. Ambas podem causar anestesia em sela.

## Membro superior

- **Erb** (tronco superior, C5-C6): *waiter's tip*. **Klumpke** (tronco inferior, C8-T1): mão em garra, às vezes síndrome de Horner.
- **Desfiladeiro torácico** (ex.: costela cervical): tronco inferior e vasos subclávios.
- Nervo **torácico longo**: **escápula alada**.
- Úmero: colo cirúrgico, **axilar**; diáfise, **radial** (mão caída); supracondiliana, **mediano**. Epicôndilo medial: **ulnar** (garra ulnar). Túnel do carpo: mediano.

## Membro inferior

- **Fibular comum** (colo da fíbula): **pé caído**.
- **Tibial**: flexão plantar fraca. **Femoral**: extensão do joelho fraca, reflexo patelar abolido.
- **Isquiático**: déficits fibulares e tibiais.
- **Glúteo superior**: **sinal de Trendelenburg**.

## Neuropatia

- **Axonal**: amplitude baixa, velocidade de condução quase normal.
- **Desmielinizante**: velocidade de condução lenta.
- Neuropatia diabética: ver o bloco de diabetes.
